name: Executive order of December 23, 1873 defining the boundaries of the Tulalip (Snohomish) Reservation
citation: Executive Order of December 23, 1873, under the Treaty of Point Elliott (January 22, 1855)
promises: The President defined the boundaries of the Tulalip or Snohomish reservation set apart by the Point Elliott treaty of January 22, 1855, running from Steamboat Slough north along section lines to the line between townships 30 and 31, then along the shores of Port Susan, Tulalip Bay and Port Gardner back to the start.
today: No court, Indian Claims Commission or congressional finding about this 1873 boundary order was found. Royce marks the order "See 351", the Point Elliott treaty cession; the Commission's Duwamish decisions (Docket 109) and its Point Elliott allocation (Docket 92) concern that treaty, which has its own record (kappler-677).

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 868
Duwamish et al. v. United States, Docket 109, Findings of Fact (5 Ind. Cl. Comm. 117, March 25, 1957)
sources.publisher: Indian Claims Commission Decisions, Oklahoma State University Library

openQuestions: treaties.json maps this record to Royce area 351. Audit 2026-11-08: Royce's Point Elliott rows put the cession at area 347 (kappler-677) and the reserves at 348 to 351; the remark beside the 36-section Tulalip reserve reads "See Executive order of Dec. 23, 1873, more specifically defining the boundaries of this reserve", so area 351 is most likely the Tulalip reserve and the map area fits this record. The researcher's earlier note that 351 is the whole cession was wrong.
presentDayTribes lists the Duwamish and Suquamish but not the Tulalip Tribes, whose reservation the order concerns.
The text of the order itself was read only in Royce's schedule; the Kappler printing was not opened.

Audit 2026-11-08: no Indian Claims Commission decision titled Tulalip was found (icc.mjs search tulalip: 0); the Snohomish dockets (125) and the Point Elliott allocation (92) concern the 1855 cession. no-breach-found kept.
